text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Sunflower and maize harvesting works are stalled due to rainfalls and farm machinery shortage.
ADEVARUL
- Government failed so far to discuss draft 1997 state budget. Budget bill will probably be debated after November polls.
TINERETUL LIBER
- Under emergency decree government revised 1996 social security budget to bring it in line with wage indexations granted this year.
ZIUA
- Parliament's lower chamber rejected bill on privatisation of commercial banks. The draft law will be rediscussed after November 3 polls.
LIBERTATEA
- Bucharest municipality plans construction of two underground parking lots in cooperation with Italian companies.
- International Bucharest fair opens on Oct 7 with over 700 Romanian companies and more than 500 foreign firms exhibiting.
- Government approved exemption from customs duties of raw materials worth 53.4 billion lei to be used in sugar making and flax and hemp production.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Auction to sell 25,000 tonnes of scrap iron from SNCFR national railway company was postponed to Nov 11 as bidders failed to meet auction terms.
General:

- All newspapers comment incident three days ago in which ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) was accused of allegedly leading a fake opinion survey aimed at shoring up lost electoral ground ahead of November 3 presidential and parliamentary polls.
ROMANIA LIBERA

- Emil Constantinescu, presidential candidate of opposition Democratic Convention (CDR) bloc leads his main rival, President Ion Iliescu in race for November 3 polls, says newspaper quoting three opinion polls conducted by major newspapers and two polling institutes.
ADEVARUL
- "Ruling PDSR threatens the voters", says editorial amid allegations the party might "sabotage" the national economy in case it loses the November 3 polls.
- One-page report evaluating activity of Bucharest's general mayor since he was elected 100 days ago.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Ion Cristoiu's editorial deals with phoney PDSR poll.
- The newspaper says PDSR pollists made calls worth 15 million lei ($4,600) a day to allegedly compromise Iliescu's main rivals in the presidential race.
TINERETUL LIBER
- Of the 95,200 foreigners found in Romania without legal documents and expired visas since November 1992, some 12,000 had been expelled, border police said.
LIBERTATEA
- Report on prostitution in the capital city of Bucharest where the police arrested several pimps and prostitues on Wednesday.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- Journalists and members of the December 21 Association of revolutionaries in December 1989 who disclosed the fake opinion survey will be investigated by the police over alleged property violation, destruction and robbery. ($=3,261 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
